summary: Session closeout skill batches Write/Edit calls too rapidly, causing approval prompt flooding and 'stream closed' errors when those tools are not in the project allow list.
evidence: 2026-04-05 session: closeout issued Write(azoth.yaml) and Write(.azoth/bootloader-state.md) in rapid succession. Both failed with 'Tool permission request failed: Error: Stream closed' — approval prompts timed out before user could respond. Root cause: closeout emits multiple file writes back-to-back with no pacing; when Write/Edit require per-call approval (not in allow list), the queue overflows the approval UI.
recommended_action: Refactor session-closeout to (1) batch state updates into a single file where possible, or (2) sequence writes with explicit checkpoints between each one, or (3) add a note in the skill instructions to add Write/Edit to settings.local.json allow list before running closeout in projects with restrictive permission models.

summary: The 'confirm before building' behavioral rule has been violated three times (ep-022, ep-028, ep-029) despite being encoded in memory. Memory-only encoding is insufficient for high-frequency, high-momentum behavioral rules — a mechanical enforcement layer is needed.
evidence: Three sessions in sequence: ep-022 (first violation, memory added), ep-028 (second violation, memory reinforced), ep-029 (third violation with memory rule present and explicit — agent still bypassed it after user said 'let's continue to the natural next step'). Pattern: after completing a task, any short forward directive triggers builder-mode bypass regardless of memory contents.
recommended_action: Implement a PreToolUse hook (scope-gate) on Write/Edit tool calls. Hook reads a session flag (.azoth/scope-gate.json) set by /plan completion. If flag absent, hook exits non-zero and prints the intent-declaration reminder. This moves the rule from agent memory (driftable) to tool execution (deterministic). New roadmap task P3-008.
